description.narrative:
Abler Nordic is a blended finance mechanism, established in 2008 as a public-private partnership, where both the MFA and Norad have been partners since inception. Abler Nordic invests in and helps build institutions providing financial inclusion to low-income households in developing countries, with a particular focus on female, small-holder farmers in rural areas. The main objective of the Technical Assistance (TA) facility in this application is to support capacity building at the Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) Abler Nordic invest in, and help mobilise private capital.
Particular attention will be paid to: - Disaster risk and climate change-related products and services focussing on the needs of small-holder farmers. - Fin-tech and mobile solutions to ensure easy access and scale, e.g., mobile and branchless banking. - Grow new and existing products, e.g., microinsurance, loans, savings, and remittances. - Internal capacity-building processes and training of clients to change people, systems, and processes/procedures that may increase efficiency and impact of services provided and improve financial and digital literacy.
Through capacity building, improved management, and strengthened focus on social performance of the MFIs, the programme aims to improve quality, operational efficiency, outreach, and private sector contributions at the Financial Services Providers (FSPs) Abler Nordic invests in. This will in turn lead to four outcomes: 1. Increased access to responsible, relevant, and affordable financial services. 2. More stable income and better resilience to climate- and other shocks. 3. Opportunity for self-employment, job-creation, and increased income. 4. Contribute to women’s economic empowerment.
